candidateAudit.text: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. Across these artistic approaches, [REVERBERATED] invites visitors to consider memory not as something simply preserved, but as something continuously produced through interactions between bodies, technologies, and environments. The exhibition thus explores how the past continues to reverberate within the systems of the present. With contributions by: Agustina Belén Agüero, Lobna Awidat, Phin Anibal, Rimon Alyagon Darr, Ronnie Danaher, Tatiana Del Valle, Hasti Ghasedi, Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz, Hanna Hofmann, Tal Horesh, Mauritius Itzinger, Laura Isselhorst, Dina Karaman, Moritz Klarer, Anna Buchner, Leonard Otterbein, David Ristić, Rajarshi Sarkar, Agnes Schyberg, Aryan Shahabian, Majedeh Shahvelayati, Mehrta Shirzadian, Pauline Simon, Laura Chalabi, People of Soil Photos: Lea Dörl

candidateAudit.text: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. candidateAudit.text: A new series of postcards is now installed at Café Exchange cafe_exchange The series was extracted from the course ‘Drawing: Here & Now’ by Simon Goritschnig zeichnungunddruckgrafik In collaborative drawing, two people share a single pen – the line becomes a space of negotiation. A play between control and letting go. Who leads – and when? Impulse meets resistance, conviction meets empathy. Not always a conversation, but always an understanding – a dance on paper. These and other experiments are part of the course “Drawing: Here & Now” by Simon Goritschnig, in which students of the department Drawing and Printmaking explore various qualities of drawing beyond observational study. In the project “Reflex,” these experimental setups are set against observational drawing. Students draw in the cashier hall of the former Postsparkasse, intuitively picking up details from architecture and space, as well as situations of coming together: conversations, movements, gazes. In this process, it becomes visible how public and social space is visually probed and explored. The focus lies on reflection — with, through, and within drawing. With contributions by: Andrea Vairelles, Anna Marino, Beth Sorby, Emilia Schönwiese, Flora Schmid, Hannah Horn, Henriette Sonntag, Leo Hasslinger, Maria Lutkova, Max Offergeld, Nikolaus Kohout, Sophie Schweizer, Anija S Dartizio, Timo Pfeifer, Vera Kügel AIL in cooperation with the department Drawing and Printmaking and Simon Goritschnig Image: Henriette Sonntag Design: Atelier Dreibholz Concept Postcard Editions and Production: Eva Weber

candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 4 Jul 2026, 15:00 The Geography of Yellow Walls Performance by Mehrta Shirzadian mehrrta Bright yellow becomes a quiet declaration of care, resistance, and return. Here, the body is reclaimed as homeland, shaped by experience rather than imposed borders. A performance unfolding through turmeric as healing material and the body as living territory. The work is rooted in a deep commitment to women’s health and critical scientific perspectives, engaging forms of embodied knowledge that have long been ignored or erased. The body becomes both evidence and memory, offering its own geography as a space of protection, defiance, and belonging. The performance is adapted to each site, responding to the spatial and contextual conditions of different venues. Mehrta Shirzadian is a performance and multimedia artist and artistic ­researcher working at the intersection of art and science. With a background in molecular biology, mathematics, and computer science, she creates participatory works exploring microbial life, sound, and bodily ecologies, addressing embodiment, agency, and the politics of representation. candidateAudit.text: On view till Saturday (18:00) – An installation presented by the department of Digital Arts / Part of Angewandte Festival René’s Collapse Collection’ is a fictional startup and alternative investment platform that explores the cultural, economic, and emotional afterlife of the collapse of René Benko’s SIGNA empire. Through NFTs, merchandise, video works, and performative sales strategies, the project examines how value is produced through speculation, narrative, and collective belief. Originally developed through public interventions, the project was expanded through a student take over by Digitale Kunst. This exhibition presents new project strands developed by the students: an NFT series reflecting on financial dependency, a merchandise collection appropriating the aesthetics of startup culture and luxury branding, and a series of short-form videos combining influencer culture, promotional performance, and social commentary. Operating at the intersection of installation, performance, and participatory fiction, Renés Collapse Collection invites visitors to engage directly with the mechanisms of speculation, value production, and collapse. A project by by Zora Hünermann and Jakob Margit With contributions by: Ulrike Fritzsche, Koschka Cosmo Keye, Juarez Suarez, Ghanishka Kedar, Sei Jeung, Ghazal Naeimi, Dongjoo Kim, Jazzmin, Margherita Pruneti, Nicolás Henao Bonnet, Roma Bogdanov, and Grisha Terno.

candidateAudit.text: In a world that is seemingly always connected, we lose ourselves in constant contact. As part of Angewandte Festival, AIL presents: Sich zusammen schreiben [to get in touch], A performance and poem by Carla Schwering and Timna Lugstein from by the department of Institute of Fine Arts & Media Art – Photography (Sophie Thun) The phrase "Schreiben wir uns zusammen" that on the surface means something like “let’s write to each other again in more detail” actually implies a postponement. In the performance, the artists type excerpts from their shared chat history in a poetic arrangement on two typewriters facing each other – messages in which they attempt to get closer to one another. The time and effort spent cancelling meet ups, for which there is supposedly no capacity is made visible. With the postcards created for the performance, visitors can reconnect with a long-lost friend. On the occasion of Angewandte Festival AIL hosts a selection of performances and installations in the cashier hall and the current exhibition will have more activations. candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 Jul 2026, 15:30 Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) Performance by Leonard Otterbein leonard.ottb The audio performance Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) explores how sound can model processes of memory formation and transformation. Layered oscillations and brief sound textures repeat with phase shifts, gradually overlapping and partially canceling each other out, much like the traces in an overwritten manuscript. The work is inspired by memory research on reconsolidation – in which recalling an event alters its stored form – and its cultural studies counterpart, reconstructivity. The piece is composed of multiple layers of sound that continuously overlap anew, attempting to cancel each other out in the process. In this process, however, the layers are never completely erased, so that fragments of the preceding states always remain Leonard Otterbein is a sound artist and composer with a background in ecology and ecotoxicology, where he studied mixture effects of agricultural pesticides and nanoparticles. His work spans instrumental and electroacoustic composition, examining perceptual thresholds. He works with psychoacoustic effects and approaches sound as spatial and sculptural material shaped by its relation to space. Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. candidateAudit.title: Nach unfassbaren 25, unheimlich schönen, sehr lehrreichen, extrem intensiven, manchmal furchtbar mühsamen, sehr feierlichen, fröhlichen, schrägen, überraschenden, ja oft auch feuch
candidateAudit.text: Nach unfassbaren 25, unheimlich schönen, sehr lehrreichen, extrem intensiven, manchmal furchtbar mühsamen, sehr feierlichen, fröhlichen, schrägen, überraschenden, ja oft auch feuchtfröhlichen, leider manchmal auch sehr traurigen, aber immer sehr menschlichen, stets emotionalen und letztendlich wunderbaren Jahren U.S.W., verlasse ich mein geliebtes Beisl nach einem 1/4 Jahrhundert. Nie hätte ich gedacht so lange dabeizusein und ich weiß nicht, ob ich es - mit heutigem Wissen - nochmal machen würde. Aber eines weiß ich: ich bin unendlich dankbar für die vielen Menschen, die ich hier kennenlernen durfte, für die vielen wertschätzenden, respektvollen, so tollen, lieben Gäste, die zu Freunden wurden und die mir so ans Herz gewachsen sind. Extrem dankbar bin ich meinen Wegbegleitern, von denen ich speziell Kerstin, Eva und Elisabeth DANKE sagen möchte, nicht zuletzt auch Reini..RIP. Danke, dass es euch gibt, danke, dass ihr mir auch zur Seite gestanden seid, wenns mal schwer war, auch mit mir persönlich. Danke an die extrem treuen Stammgäste. Ihr seid alle der Wahnsinn! ❤️❤️❤️❤️ Das U.S.W. wird weitergehen. Ich werde mich neuen Projekten widmen, davor mal alles verarbeiten und mal mein Telefon nachts abschalten. Kommt alle am 30.5. vorbei. Ich freu mich auf jeden von euch! Und alle die es nicht schaffen: Am 27.5. findet das letzte Quiz unter meiner "Regie" statt. Es wird mein etwa 1250. sein. 😱 Wer auch das nicht schafft, schaffts davor, dazwischen oder danach. Allen anderen: Danke, es war mir eine Ehre. Macht's gut! ❤️

candidateAudit.title: Liebe Mitglieder, liebe Freunde, liebe Alle, "wenn ihr wollt, ist es kein Märchen" - unter diesem Motto haben wir ohne Übertreibung jahrelang für eine Rückkehr zu unserem Biotop, d
candidateAudit.text: Liebe Mitglieder, liebe Freunde, liebe Alle, "wenn ihr wollt, ist es kein Märchen" - unter diesem Motto haben wir ohne Übertreibung jahrelang für eine Rückkehr zu unserem Biotop, dem 2. Bezirk, auch Mazzesinsel genannt, gekämpft. Ab 1. Juli wird Maccabi erstmals in seiner 55jährigen Geschichte auf einen Platz den gesamten Spielbetrieb veranstalten, also Trainings- und Meisterschaftsbetrieb. Zu verdanken ist dies der Kooperation mit dem SK Rapid, der uns als Mieter das Kunstrasenfeld innerhalb des Rapid-Trainingszentrums zur Verfügung stellt. Durch die Magistratsabteilung MA 51 der Stadt Wien werden unmittelbar neben dem Spielfeld eine Container-Landschaft errichtet, die uns als Kabinen mit angeschlossenen Sanitäreinrichtungen in der Zukunft dienen. Wir verweisen mit großem Stolz auf diesen Sieg abseits des grünen (Kunst)Rasens - nun liegt es an uns und euch, um die nächsten Ziele zu erreichen: - Kinder- und Jugend-Mannschaften in allen Jahrgängen - Anmerkung: für die kommende Saison 2025/26 wurden eine U7 (Jahrgang 2019 und jünger), U8, U10, U11, U12, U15 sowie U18 (Jahrgang 2007/08) beim WFV (Wiener Fußball Verband) zum Meisterschaftsbetrieb angemeldet - die Erwachsenen-Teams, Kampfmannschaft und U23, konsolidieren - rund um das jüdische Biotop, bestehend aus ZPC-Schule, Hakoah und nun dem Fußballplatz, soll ein offenes Sportzentrum entstehen, das Schritt für Schritt entwickelt wird. In diesem Sinne: KADIMA Maccabi!
